author: reek
body: The control half of the runtime scope experiment. This program declares no filesystem scope, so its grant is unscoped and every path is admitted -- the empty prefix admits everything, which is what an unscoped grant means.

author: reek
body: It writes NO.TXT, reads it back, and lists the root, and all three work. Its twin, scope-runtime-deny, is the SAME three operations on the SAME blank disk with the SAME code, and the only difference between the two programs is a scope literal in the effect row. That is what makes the twin's three refusals evidence of the scope and not of a broken filesystem: without this half, a denial and a bug are the same picture.
